purpose: Qualify Request-to-Pay as a request/messaging lifecycle distinct from payment initiation, execution and settlement.

source_register.title: PayShap Request product page
supports: Capitec product page describes sending and accepting PayShap Requests through its app
Page observed 2026-11-04 lists R100 per request and two requests per 24 hours with R200 combined limit
Page says payment follows once payer accepts the request
does_not_support: Effective date for the displayed limit change
Universal PayShap Request limits across participants
Settlement/finality from the request acceptance event alone

does_not_support: Current 2026 account limit
Effective date of any change
Universal pricing for all participants

Scheme defines roles and operating rules for request initiation messages

Banking payment execution or settlement outcome

Settlement finality

South African product rules

source_register.title: PayShap Request FAQ
supports: The FAQ says sending a PayShap Request is free and a fee is charged when the request is received/approved, based on amount.
The FAQ lists payer fee bands of R0-R100 free, R100.01-R1000 R1, and R1000.01-R3000 R3.50.
The same FAQ says the maximum requested amount is R100 per transaction and a customer can make two requests per day or within 24 hours to any South African bank.
The FAQ describes a pending request as cancellable by the sender, a default one-day expiry, and decline without money being taken.
The FAQ says the request carries the sender name and reference, and acceptance triggers an immediate, irrevocable payment.
The FAQ says the request includes the sender's name and reference, while telling users to decline if they do not know who sent it or why.
The FAQ says only logged-in users can send or approve requests in the Capitec app.
The FAQ says the requester can cancel a sent request if the person has already paid, and that the request has an expiry date.
does_not_support: An effective date for the displayed limits or fee schedule.
A universal rule or fee schedule for every PayShap Request participant.
A reconciled interpretation of fee bands above R100 when the same FAQ caps request amounts at R100.
A guarantee that sender authentication establishes that the underlying request or asserted debt is legitimate.
That the displayed sender name cryptographically identifies the legal person, proves the sender has authority to collect for the named beneficiary, or validates the underlying invoice/debt.

source_register.title: Verification of Payee Scheme Rulebook v1.1
supports: VOP v1.1 is effective 20 September 2026.
Requesting PSP asks responding PSP to check an IBAN and payee name or eligible identifier; response can be match, close match, no match or check not possible.
The scheme concerns account/name verification before SCT or SCT Inst payment initiation.
does_not_support: The EPC says VOP messaging cannot be relied upon to identify a private or legal person.
A matching account name does not establish invoice legitimacy, collect authority, absence of account compromise, or voluntariness of a payment request.
South African PayShap/PayShap Request participant conformance or law.

source_register.title: EPC Recommendations for VOP matching processes v2.0
supports: Version 2.0 published 3 November 2026 addresses character sets and match outcomes for natural and legal persons.
Guidance discusses spelling differences, transposed letters, initials, phonetic variations, commercial names and accepted abbreviations.
Responding PSP remains responsible for its matching outcome and may apply its own criteria.
does_not_support: That a close/match response proves the underlying request is legitimate or the account operator is acting voluntarily.
South African ShapID matching rules or participant-specific limits.

source_register.title: PayShap Request product and FAQ
supports: Absa page says sent requests to other banks are limited to R50,000 per transaction; Absa-to-Absa ShapID requests up to R3,000; on-us account-number requests up to R5 million.
Absa says senders may send unlimited requests per day but at most five to the same recipient per day; recipients may receive unlimited total requests but at most five from the same sender per day.
Absa states requests sent by Absa expire after 45 days.
Absa permits payers to accept or decline; partial/reduced payment is available when the sender enabled the Amount Modification Indicator.
Absa limits PayShap to domestic South African transactions and describes app-based request flow.
does_not_support: A guarantee that a request is legitimate merely because it is delivered in the Absa app.
A fee schedule for the PayShap Request flow.
A default expiry shorter than the stated 45-day period.
The same limits for requests sent from other participants or every off-us recipient bank.

source_register.title: PayShap Request FAQs
supports: Nedbank says PayShap Requests can be up to R50,000 per transaction per day, subject to potentially lower limits at other banks.
Nedbank states no daily limit on the number of PayShap Requests that can be sent or paid.
Nedbank sets a 14-day default request expiry, configurable to a date between the current day and 45 days from creation.
Nedbank says a payer may decline, a decline closes the request and it cannot later be accepted; the requester is notified of the decline reason.
Nedbank says a cancelled request is closed and cannot be resent.
does_not_support: A universal PayShap request limit across other participants.
A fee schedule specific to the Request flow.
Partial-payment availability.
A legal conclusion about the underlying debt or the legitimacy of a request.

profiles.fee_note: FAQ says requester fee is zero and the payer/approver pays amount-based fees; the same FAQ caps requests at R100 but lists additional payer-fee bands above R100. Preserve the mismatch; do not infer an applicable fee above the stated cap. The FAQ does not state a separate combined daily-value cap; leave that field unknown rather than deriving one.

integer numeric values only; floating-point values forbidden
null and booleans use their lowercase JSON literals
